title: 141. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Interpreting Energy Units and Conversion
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Convert energy from kilojoules to joules.
questions.question: Convert \(2\text{ kJ}\) to joules.
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ kJ}=1{,}000\text{ J}\), multiply \(2\) by \(1{,}000\): \(2\times 1{,}000=2{,}000\). Therefore, \(2\text{ kJ}=2{,}000\text{ J}\). Option B incorrectly uses \(100\text{ J}\) per kilojoule.
questions.hint: Recall how many joules the prefix kilo- represents.

questions.learningObjective: Convert energy from joules to kilojoules.
questions.question: Convert \(500\text{ J}\) to kilojoules.
questions.explanation: Since \(1{,}000\text{ J}=1\text{ kJ}\), divide \(500\) by \(1{,}000\): \(500\div 1{,}000=0.5\). Therefore, \(500\text{ J}=0.5\text{ kJ}\). Option B incorrectly divides by \(100\).
questions.hint: Keep track of the metric prefix before converting the energy value.

questions.learningObjective: Convert energy from kilowatt-hours to joules.
questions.question: Convert \(1\text{ kWh}\) to joules.
questions.explanation: Use \(1\text{ kW}=1{,}000\text{ W}\) and \(1\text{ h}=3{,}600\text{ s}\). The numerical conversion factor is \(1{,}000\times 3{,}600=3{,}600{,}000\), giving \(1\text{ kWh}=3.6\times 10^6\text{ J}\). The alternative loses one factor of ten in the hour-to-second conversion.
questions.hint: For a powered device, combine its power with its operating duration.

questions.learningObjective: Convert energy from kilocalories to joules.
questions.question: Convert \(1\text{ kcal}\) to joules using \(1\text{ cal}=4.184\text{ J}\).
questions.explanation: Use \(1\text{ kcal}=1{,}000\text{ cal}\) and \(1\text{ cal}=4.184\text{ J}\). The numerical conversion is \(1{,}000\times 4.184=4{,}184\), giving \(1\text{ kcal}=4{,}184\text{ J}\). The alternative omits the kilo prefix and gives the energy in one calorie.
questions.hint: Convert kilocalories to calories first, then apply the given joules-per-calorie factor.

questions.learningObjective: Convert energy from kilowatt-hours to megajoules.
questions.question: Convert \(2.5\text{ kWh}\) to megajoules.
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ kWh}=3.6\times 10^6\text{ J}=3.6\text{ MJ}\), multiply \(2.5\) by \(3.6\): \(2.5\times 3.6=9\). Therefore, \(2.5\text{ kWh}=9\text{ MJ}\). Option B is ten times too small.
questions.hint: Keep track of the metric prefix before converting the energy value.

questions.learningObjective: Convert energy from joules to kilowatt-hours.
questions.question: Convert \(10{,}000\text{ J}\) to kilowatt-hours. Round to three significant figures.
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ kWh}=3.6\times 10^6\text{ J}\), divide \(10{,}000\) by \(3.6\times 10^6\): \(\frac{10{,}000}{3{,}600{,}000}\approx 0.00278\), which is \(2.78\times 10^{-3}\text{ kWh}\). Therefore, \(10{,}000\text{ J}\approx 2.78\times 10^{-3}\text{ kWh}\). Option B is ten times too large.
questions.hint: Recall how many joules make one kilowatt-hour, then decide whether to multiply or divide.

questions.learningObjective: Convert energy from calories to joules.
questions.question: Convert \(500\text{ cal}\) to joules using \(1\text{ cal}=4.184\text{ J}\).
questions.explanation: Multiply \(500\) by \(4.184\): \(500\times 4.184=2{,}092\). Therefore, \(500\text{ cal}=2{,}092\text{ J}\). Option A is ten times too small.
questions.hint: Each calorie corresponds to the given number of joules; decide whether to multiply or divide.

questions.learningObjective: Convert energy from megajoules to kilowatt-hours.
questions.question: Convert \(3.6\text{ MJ}\) to kilowatt-hours.
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ kWh}=3.6\text{ MJ}\), \(3.6\text{ MJ}\) is exactly \(1\text{ kWh}\). Therefore, \(3.6\text{ MJ}=1\text{ kWh}\). Option B is ten times too large.
questions.hint: Keep track of the metric prefix before converting the energy value.

questions.learningObjective: Convert energy from joules to calories.
questions.question: Convert \(1{,}000\text{ J}\) to calories using \(1\text{ cal}=4.184\text{ J}\), rounded to the nearest calorie.
questions.explanation: Divide \(1{,}000\) by \(4.184\): \(\frac{1{,}000}{4.184}\approx 239.0\). Therefore, \(1{,}000\text{ J}\approx 239\text{ cal}\). Option A is ten times too large.
questions.hint: Each calorie corresponds to the given number of joules, so converting from joules to calories reverses that conversion.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate energy in joules from power and time.
questions.question: A device uses \(500\text{ W}\) of power for \(2\text{ h}\). How much energy does it use in joules?
questions.explanation: The energy is \(500\text{ W}\times 2\text{ h}=1{,}000\text{ Wh}=1\text{ kWh}\). Since \(1\text{ kWh}=3.6\times 10^6\text{ J}\), the energy is \(3.6\times 10^6\text{ J}\). Option A incorrectly treats watt-hours as joules directly.
questions.hint: Identify the energy unit and any time conversion involved.
